name: john-otienoh/Aviation_OTP_Pipeline
what_it_holds: Containerized Airflow + PostgreSQL pipeline computing industry-standard aviation on-time-performance reliability metrics from BTS On-Time Performance CSVs; ships only a 100-row synthetic prototype file (bts_ontime_simulated.csv, Jan2022-Dec2024 range simulated) — real BTS data is user-downloaded and gitignored above 100MB. MIT licensed, early-stage (3 commits).
why_useful: A ready-made ETL scaffold (Airflow DAG + Postgres schema) for ingesting monthly BTS OTP files on a recurring basis, which could shortcut building a repeatable pull for a live delay/capacity monitor; data itself is not included so value is purely as tooling.
time_coverage: Pipeline designed for any month; prototype simulates Jan2022-Dec2024
size_hint: Prototype ships 100 rows only; real data external

name: lienas/us-flight-delays-eda
what_it_holds: EDA notebooks over a ~2 million-row / ~644k-flight sample of BTS On-Time domestic flight data spanning 2010-2019 (22 reporting carriers); raw airline_2m.csv (~880MB) not committed (exceeds GitHub's 100MB limit) — README points to the official BTS On-Time archive for the download. No 2020+ data (COVID-affected 2020 explicitly excluded).
why_useful: A worked decade-long (2010-2019) carrier-level delay panel definition that could be re-pulled and extended through 2026 from the same BTS On-Time archive if a longer historical baseline for airline capacity/reliability is needed; itself contributes no new data since the file isn't committed and stops in 2019.
